headline.technical: AI-trade doubts hit Asian tech: KOSPI -6.16%, TAIEX -4.80%, Nikkei 225 -2.78%, while Nifty 50 rose 1.85% on foreign inflows and lower crude.
headline.layman: Worries about the AI boom hit tech stocks hard in Asia today. India went the other way and rose, helped by foreign money and cheaper oil.

global.title: AI-trade doubts drive a global tech sell-off

status.technical: Risk-off led by Asian tech: KOSPI -6.16%, TAIEX -4.80%, Nikkei 225 -2.78%. Nasdaq Composite closed -1.48%; VIX 29.29, +11.12% on the day. The Financial Times said the Nasdaq 100 was set to open lower as a weeks-long sell-off continues.
status.layman: Tech shares fell sharply in Asia. The US Nasdaq also fell 1.48%. The VIX, Wall Street's fear gauge, rose to 29.29. The Financial Times says the tech sell-off has lasted weeks.

consequence.technical: If AI-trade doubts persist, funding and sentiment could stay under pressure: CNBC reported lenders are becoming pickier on corporate bonds for the AI build-out, and Bloomberg said Treasuries rose across the curve as AI concerns dented risk sentiment. Reuters said Nasdaq futures slid over 2% on fresh US tariff concerns.
consequence.layman: If worry about AI spending keeps growing, borrowing for big tech projects could get harder. CNBC says lenders are getting pickier. Bloomberg says investors moved into US government bonds. Reuters says Nasdaq futures fell over 2% on tariff fears.

impact.technical: Korean, Taiwanese and Japanese chip and tech holders are most exposed: Samsung Electronics -9.87% and SK Hynix -11.05% (1d). Bitcoin funds are headed for their worst month since June 2022 with outflows near US$5 billion (Straits Times); gold is near 15-month lows on Fed hike bets (Investing.com).
impact.layman: People holding Korean, Taiwanese and Japanese tech shares are hit most. Bitcoin funds are having their worst month since June 2022, with outflows near US$5 billion, says the Straits Times. Gold is near 15-month lows.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary S&P 500 days the next day rose 54% of 844 times and the next 5 days rose 59% of 843 times. After a KOSPI one-day fall bigger than one standard deviation, the next 5 days rose 51% of 152 times. Volatility is elevated (S&P 500 20-day volatility 31.8%).
outlook.layman: History is not a forecast. After ordinary S&P 500 days, the next day was up 54% of 844 times. The next 5 days were up 59% of 843 times. Swings are big right now, so surprises in either direction are normal.

regions.title: Americas: tech weighs, Dow edges up

status.technical: S&P 500 -0.50%, Nasdaq Composite -1.48%, Dow +0.85%. Of the largest Nasdaq names only 2 of 8 rose; Nvidia -5.86% and Broadcom -3.98%. The Straits Times said Nasdaq and S&P 500 slipped after Nvidia's rally. The TSX ended lower as tech and mining shares fell (Mint).
status.layman: US tech shares fell while the Dow rose 0.85%. The S&P 500 slipped 0.50% and the Nasdaq 1.48%. Nvidia dropped 5.86%. Canada's main index also ended lower as tech and mining stocks fell.

consequence.technical: If new US tariffs arrive as Investing.com reports Trump is set to add, and China warns against them (Straits Times), risk appetite could stay fragile. Reuters said Nasdaq futures slid over 2% on tariff concerns.
consequence.layman: If the US adds new tariffs, as Investing.com reports, markets could stay nervous. China has warned the US against it, says the Straits Times.

impact.technical: Tech-heavy Nasdaq holders are most exposed; the Dow's mix held up better (Home Depot +2.20%, UnitedHealth +1.73%). Dell fell after earnings that Yahoo Finance called a blowout. Deutsche Bank's Binky Chadha is among the biggest S&P 500 bulls with a 9,000 target (Bloomberg).
impact.layman: Tech-heavy portfolios took the hit. Dell fell even after strong results, says Yahoo Finance. Deutsche Bank's Binky Chadha remains a big bull on the S&P 500, with a 9,000 target, says Bloomberg.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary Nasdaq days the next day rose 55% of 824 times and the next 5 days rose 59% of 823 times; for the S&P 500 the next day rose 54% of 844 times.
outlook.layman: History is not a forecast. After ordinary Nasdaq days, the next day was up 55% of 824 times and the next 5 days were up 59% of 823 times.

regions.title: Europe: steady after the US tech tumble

status.technical: CAC 40 +0.98%, FTSE 100 +0.41%, DAX +0.17%, Euro Stoxx 50 -0.01%. Morningstar said Europe perked up after the US tech tumble. Eurozone bond yields tracked Treasury yields lower (WSJ).
status.layman: European stocks were mostly steady. France's CAC 40 rose 0.98% and Britain's FTSE 100 rose 0.41%. Morningstar says Europe perked up after the US tech fall. Bond yields fell.

consequence.technical: If inflation keeps surprising, the ECB may tighten further: Bloomberg reported Governing Council member Martin Kocher said the ECB can't fall behind the curve and suggested he'd back further rate increases. The ECB deposit facility rate is 2.5 %.
consequence.layman: If prices keep rising faster than hoped, the European Central Bank may raise rates again. ECB member Martin Kocher said the bank can't fall behind, says Bloomberg. The deposit rate is 2.5 %.

impact.technical: Ofgem said British household energy bills will soar 26% from January on higher wholesale gas costs (Financial Times), which pressures UK households. Evidence on sector effects in the notes is thin.
impact.layman: UK households face a 26% jump in energy bills from January, says the Financial Times, because wholesale gas costs rose. The notes say little else about who is affected.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary Euro Stoxx 50 days the next day rose 53% of 847 times and the next 5 days rose 57% of 846 times.
outlook.layman: History is not a forecast. After ordinary Euro Stoxx 50 days, the next day was up 53% of 847 times, and the next 5 days were up 57% of 846 times.

regions.title: Asia-Pacific: AI sell-off, India bucks the trend

status.technical: KOSPI -6.16%, TAIEX -4.80%, Nikkei 225 -2.78%, Shenzhen Component -3.24%, Shanghai Composite -2.03%; Nifty 50 +1.85%. Business Standard said MSCI's Asia-Pacific ex-Japan index was down 3.2% on AI-rebound and US tariff worries. Bloomberg said Taiwan stocks tumbled 8% as the Huang boost faded.
status.layman: Asian markets fell hard. South Korea dropped 6.16%, Taiwan 4.80% and Japan 2.78%. Chinese markets also fell. India rose 1.85%. Business Standard says worries about AI and US tariffs drove the fall.

consequence.technical: If the AI sell-off continues, chip makers could stay under pressure. Mainland exchanges cut trading thresholds to stem the decline (SCMP). Foreign investors put $13 billion into Indian stocks over 14 sessions after two months of outflows (Mint).
consequence.layman: If AI worries last, chip makers may stay under pressure. China's exchanges are easing trading rules to slow the fall, says the SCMP. Foreign investors put $13 billion into Indian stocks in 14 sessions, says Mint.

impact.technical: Samsung Electronics -9.87% and SK Hynix -11.05% weighed on KOSPI; SoftBank Group -14.83% and Tokyo Electron -12.53% on the Nikkei; CATL -8.33% on Shenzhen. SCMP said Chinese private funds retreated from record highs as AI bubble jitters hit Nvidia backers.
impact.layman: Big chip names fell sharply. Samsung dropped 9.87% and SK Hynix 11.05%. SoftBank fell 14.83%. The SCMP says Chinese private funds pulled back as fears of an AI bubble grew.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after one-day falls bigger than one standard deviation, the next 5 days rose 51% of 152 times for KOSPI and 45% of 167 times for the Shenzhen Component. After rises that large, the Nifty 50's next 5 days rose 62% of 174 times.
outlook.layman: History is not a forecast. After big one-day falls, KOSPI was up over the next 5 days 51% of 152 times. Shenzhen was up 45% of 167 times. After big rises, the Nifty 50 was up 62% of 174 times.

status.technical: Financial Times: tech stocks slide as confidence in the AI trade fades. Business Standard: Asian stocks tumbled as the AI rebound stumbled. Nasdaq Composite -1.48%, VIX 29.29.
status.layman: Investors are losing confidence in the AI boom, says the Financial Times. Tech shares have been sliding for weeks. The Nasdaq fell 1.48% and the VIX rose to 29.29.

consequence.technical: If lenders stay picky, CNBC says Big Tech could find it tougher to raise debt for the AI build-out. If Nvidia-linked sentiment sours further, Chinese private funds that backed it could retreat more (SCMP).
consequence.layman: If lenders stay picky, big tech firms may find it harder to borrow for AI projects, says CNBC. Funds that backed Nvidia in China have already pulled back, says the SCMP.

impact.technical: Semiconductor-heavy indices in Korea and Taiwan are hit hardest: Samsung Electronics -9.87%, SK Hynix -11.05%. The notes give little detail on effects beyond tech.
impact.layman: Chip-heavy markets in Korea and Taiwan are hit hardest. Samsung fell 9.87%. The notes say little about other sectors.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary Nasdaq days the next 5 days rose 59% of 823 times.
outlook.layman: History is not a forecast: after ordinary Nasdaq days, the next 5 days were up 59% of 823 times.

status.technical: Investing.com reported Trump is set to add new sweeping tariffs; China warned the US against new tariffs (Straits Times). Reuters said Nasdaq futures slid over 2% on fresh tariff concerns.
status.layman: Investing.com says Trump plans new sweeping tariffs. China warned the US not to do it, says the Straits Times. Reuters says Nasdaq futures fell over 2%.

consequence.technical: If tariffs are imposed, WSJ-reported Chinese suspension of some critical-material export curbs to the US until January could be at risk; the notes do not say so directly. Metals buyers face uncertainty: WSJ said tariff uncertainty clouded the global demand outlook for copper.
consequence.layman: If new tariffs arrive, trade tensions could rise again. WSJ says tariff uncertainty already clouds demand for copper. China has paused some export limits on critical materials until January.

impact.technical: Exporters and metals markets are exposed; copper is down 18.36% over a month. Evidence on specific companies is thin.
impact.layman: Exporters and metal markets are most exposed. Copper has fallen 18.36% in a month. The notes name few specific firms.

outlook.technical: Base rates, not predictions: after ordinary copper days the next 5 days rose 54% of 861 times.
outlook.layman: History is not a forecast: after ordinary copper days, the next 5 days were up 54% of 861 times.

status.technical: Investing.com: gold holds near 15-month lows on Fed hike bets, PCE inflation awaited. Mint: higher US yields and a stronger dollar pressured precious metals. US 10-year yield 4.90, dollar index 104.01. Bloomberg: BOJ's faster inflation indicator backs the case for another hike.
status.layman: Investors are betting the Fed may raise rates, says Investing.com. That has pushed gold near 15-month lows. The US 10-year yield is 4.90. Bloomberg says Japan's central bank may raise rates again.

consequence.technical: If a prolonged higher-for-longer policy regime takes hold, Business Standard says gold faces more pressure. ECB's Kocher suggested he'd back further hikes (Bloomberg).
consequence.layman: If rates stay high for long, gold may stay under pressure, says Business Standard. ECB member Martin Kocher said he'd back more rate hikes, says Bloomberg.

impact.technical: Gold holders have felt it most: gold is -12.76% over one month. Mint also says analysts see gold and silver as deeply oversold but warn further declines remain possible.
impact.layman: Gold owners feel it most. Gold is down 12.76% in a month. Mint says analysts see gold and silver as oversold, but more falls are possible.

outlook.layman: History is not a forecast: after ordinary gold days, the next 5 days were up 55% of 850 times.

status.technical: Brent crude closed at 88.07, -3.64% on the day. Bloomberg: Houthi gains in Yemen expand the Gulf's second front as Saudi Arabia is attacked. Reuters: Gulf bourses mixed after Saudi attacks. Al Jazeera: Iran rations electricity.
status.layman: Oil fell 3.64% to 88.07 a barrel for Brent. Meanwhile conflict in the Gulf region continues. Reuters says Saudi Arabia was attacked and Gulf markets were mixed.

consequence.technical: If crude keeps slipping, Business Standard says oil-sensitive stocks in India could keep rallying. If Gulf attacks escalate, Bloomberg says UAE plans suggest infrastructure in the Persian Gulf is seen as vulnerable.
consequence.layman: If oil keeps falling, oil-sensitive Indian shares may keep rising, says Business Standard. Bloomberg says the UAE sees its Gulf infrastructure as vulnerable.

impact.technical: Indian importers and oil-sensitive stocks benefit from cheaper crude (Business Standard); Brent is -22.66% over one month. UK households face higher gas-linked bills (Financial Times).
impact.layman: Indian firms that use lots of oil benefit from cheaper crude. Brent is down 22.66% in a month. UK homes face higher energy bills, says the Financial Times.

outlook.layman: History is not a forecast: after big one-day Brent falls, the next 5 days were up 53% of 171 times.

status.technical: Mint: foreign investors poured $13 billion into Indian equities over 14 sessions, reversing September and October outflows. Nifty 50 +1.85%, Sensex +1.82%. Business Standard: Indian markets surged 10 per cent in November.
status.layman: Foreign investors put $13 billion into Indian stocks over 14 sessions, says Mint. India's Nifty 50 rose 1.85% and the Sensex 1.82%. The rupee also strengthened.

consequence.technical: If markets stay buoyant, Business Standard cites Kotak Institutional Equities warning that the sharp November run-up dims the risk-reward ratio and volatility is likely.
consequence.layman: After such a quick rise, Business Standard says risk and reward look less attractive and more ups and downs are likely.

impact.layman: Mint says 14 sectors got foreign money. The rupee hit an eight-month high, closing at 92.23 per dollar, says the Economic Times.
